items.stem: Describe the three early satyagraha movements of Gandhiji in India.
items.answer: (1) Champaran (1917): against the indigo plantation system. (2) Kheda (1917): for relaxation of revenue after crop failure. (3) Ahmedabad (1918): for cotton mill workers.

items.stem:
Read the source (adapted from an account of 13 April 1919) and answer the questions.
"On the day of Baisakhi, a large crowd gathered in an enclosed ground. Some had come to protest against new repressive measures, others to attend a fair. Many were villagers unaware of the martial law. The commanding officer blocked the exits and ordered his men to open fire."
(i) Name the place and the city where this happened. (1 mark)
(ii) Which officer gave the order to fire? (1 mark)
(iii) Give two ways in which Indians reacted to the incident. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar. (ii) General Dyer. (iii) Crowds came out on strike and clashed with police; Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood; the movement against British rule spread.

items.stem: Why did Gandhiji decide to take up the Khilafat issue?
items.answer: (1) He wanted to bring Hindus and Muslims together in a broad movement. (2) The harsh peace treaty on the Ottoman emperor angered Muslims. (3) He felt no broad-based movement could succeed without Hindu-Muslim unity.

items.stem:
Read the source (adapted from Gandhiji's letter to the Viceroy, 1930) and answer the questions.
"The British system seems designed to crush the poor. Even salt, which the poor need to live, is taxed so that the burden falls heaviest on them. If you cannot remove these evils and my letter makes no appeal to your heart, I shall proceed with such co-workers of the Ashram as I can take to disregard the provisions of the Salt Laws."
(i) To whom was this letter written? (1 mark)
(ii) Which movement began after the demands were not met? (1 mark)
(iii) Why did Gandhiji think the salt tax hurt the poor most? Give two reasons. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Lord Irwin, the Viceroy. (ii) The Civil Disobedience Movement (Salt March to Dandi). (iii) Salt was an essential food item used by all; the tax and the government monopoly raised its price, which hit the poor hardest.
items.markingKey: (i) 1 mark: Lord Irwin, the Viceroy. (ii) 1 mark: The Civil Disobedience Movement (Salt March to Dandi). (iii) 2 marks: Salt was an essential food item used by all; the tax and the government monopoly raised its price, which hit the poor hardest.

items.stem:
(a) Compare the way peasants of Awadh and tribal people of the Gudem Hills participated in the Non-Cooperation Movement. (3 marks)
(b) Why did the Non-Cooperation Movement in the towns slow down? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) Awadh peasants struggled against talukdars and landlords for reduced revenue and abolition of begar. (2) They organised nai-dhobi bandhs. (3) Gudem tribals, led by Alluri Sitaram Raju, used guerrilla warfare against restrictions on forests. (4) Both interpreted swaraj in their own way, sometimes going beyond non-violence. (b) (1) Khadi cloth was more expensive than mill cloth and poor people could not afford it. (2) Alternative Indian institutions were slow to come up, so students and teachers returned to government schools.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) Awadh peasants struggled against talukdars and landlords for reduced revenue and abolition of begar. (2) They organised nai-dhobi bandhs. (3) Gudem tribals, led by Alluri Sitaram Raju, used guerrilla warfare against restrictions on forests. (4) Both interpreted swaraj in their own way, sometimes going beyond non-violence. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) Khadi cloth was more expensive than mill cloth and poor people could not afford it. (2) Alternative Indian institutions were slow to come up, so students and teachers returned to government schools.

items.stem:
(a) Why did many Muslims feel alienated from the Congress after the Non-Cooperation–Khilafat movement? (3 marks)
(b) Why did Ambedkar demand separate electorates for dalits? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) The Congress came to be associated with Hindu religious nationalist groups like the Hindu Mahasabha. (2) Communal clashes worsened relations. (3) The All Parties Conference of 1928 failed when the Hindu Mahasabha opposed compromise. (4) The question of representation in assemblies remained unresolved. (b) (1) He believed political empowerment would resolve the problems of their social disabilities. (2) Dalits would choose their own representatives.
items.markingKey: (a) any three points, 1 mark each: (1) The Congress came to be associated with Hindu religious nationalist groups like the Hindu Mahasabha. (2) Communal clashes worsened relations. (3) The All Parties Conference of 1928 failed when the Hindu Mahasabha opposed compromise. (4) The question of representation in assemblies remained unresolved. (b) any two points, 1 mark each: (1) He believed political empowerment would resolve the problems of their social disabilities. (2) Dalits would choose their own representatives.

(a) Why did Gandhiji decide to take up the Khilafat issue? (3 marks)
(b) Why did the First World War create a new economic and political situation in India? (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) (1) He wanted to bring Hindus and Muslims together in a broad movement. (2) The harsh peace treaty on the Ottoman emperor angered Muslims. (3) He felt no broad-based movement could succeed without Hindu-Muslim unity. (b) (1) Defence expenditure rose and was financed by loans and higher taxes, including income tax. (2) Prices doubled and forced recruitment in villages caused widespread anger.
